newsitem.title: THAILAND: UN launches emergency rice aid for Laos.
newsitem.headline: UN launches emergency rice aid for Laos.

text.p: The U.N. World Food Programme (WFP) said on Thursday it had launched an emergency operation to raise 30,240 tonnes of rice for flood victims in Laos.

"The food will help the more than 420,000 flood victims -- all subsistence farmers growing a single crop per year -- survive in their villages and cultivate this year's rice crop during the six months leading up to the next harvest in November 1997," the WFP said in a statement.
The agency estimated about 43,000 tonnes of rice would be needed for those hit by devastating floods that struck central Laos last September and wiped out crops.
The WFP said it hoped the remainder of the rice required would be raised from donors, either given directly to the Laotian government or through the WFP.
The land-locked nation suffered severe floods in 1991, drought in 1992 and 1993, and floods again in 1994 and 1995.
About 80 percent of the population is dependent on agriculture and 81 percent of the land under cultivation is used to grow rice.
